rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads the three verbs ‘they conceal, reveal, and call upon’ with third-person yāʾ throughout.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم يسرون ويعلنون ويدعون كلها بالياء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads يدعون in the third person but تسرون and تعلنون in the second person.
rows.anchor: يدعون } بالياء خاصة على المغايبة وتسرون وتعلنون بالتاء على الخطاب

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use second-person tāʾ forms throughout, coordinating these verbs with the preceding address.
rows.anchor: والباقون كلها بالتاء على الخطاب عطفا على ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second phrase adds that idols are themselves created by another, beyond the preceding statement that they create nothing; both expose their deficiencies.
rows.anchor: أنهم لا يخلقون شيئا وأنهم مخلوقون لغيرهم ، فكان هذا زيادة في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are dead rather than living; a true deity must be alive without ever dying, whereas idols have the opposite condition.
rows.anchor: لو كانت آلهة على الحقيقة لكانوا أحياء غير أموات ، أي غير جائز عليها الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them dead and not living distinguishes God, whose life is never followed by death, from idols whose death is never followed by life.
rows.anchor: الإله هو الحي الذي لا يحصل عقيب حياته موت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added wording repeats the idea deliberately for idolaters whose extreme ignorance may require several expressions to grasp one meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن تكلم مع الجاهل الغر الغبي فقد يحسن أن يعبر عن المعنى الواحد بالعبارات الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a general warning against breaking covenants and oaths, this verse addresses particular pledges the listeners had made, avoiding a pointless repetition.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد منه التحذير عن نقض مطلق الإيمان ، وإلا لزم التكرير الخالي عن الفائدة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes identify the specific pledges as the pledge to the Messenger, which required belief in him and his law.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : المراد من هذه الآية نهي الذين بايعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slipping foot after firmness is a proverb for falling into distress after well-being; breaking Islam's covenant drops one from high rank into error.
rows.anchor: مثل يذكر لكل من وقع في بلاء بعد عافية ، فإن من نقض عهد الإسلام فقد سقط عن الدرجات العالية

words: وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The evil’ means punishment, and ‘because you barred’ means because you turned people away from God's path; the punishment is severe.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك السوء الذي تذوقونه سوء عظيم وعقاب شديد

words: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small price means worldly benefit, however plentiful; remaining in Islam is better than any worldly gain offered for breaking its covenant, if one knows the difference.
rows.anchor: يريد عرض الدنيا وإن كان كثيرا ، إلا أن ما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sense shows worldly goods end, while reason shows afterlife goods endure; the enduring is better than the finite, making this a decisive proof of the afterlife's superiority.
rows.anchor: الحس شاهد بأن خيرات الدنيا منقطعة ، والعقل دل على أن خيرات الآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من المنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a worldly blessing is noble, knowing it will end spoils its enjoyment and its loss intensifies grief; if it is base, an enduring good is plainly better.
rows.anchor: العلم بأنه سينقطع يجعله منغصا حال حصوله ، وأما حال حصول ذلك الانقطاع فإنها تعظم الحسرة والحزن

rows.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
rows.claim: Jahm b. Ṣafwān says the bliss of Paradise ends; al-Rāzī treats the verse's statement that what is with God remains as proof against him.
rows.anchor: وقال جهم بن صفوان : إنه منقطع والآية حجة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith binds a believer both to remain steadfast in Islam without reverting and to perform all the obligations and requirements of its law.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يصبر على ذلك الالتزام وأن لا يرجع عنه وأن لا ينقضه بعد ثبوته

words: وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا۟ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encourages steadfastness in Islam by rewarding the patient according to their best deeds; people earn reward for recommended and obligatory acts, not merely permitted acts.
rows.anchor: يجزيهم على أحسن أعمالهم ، وذلك لأن المؤمن قد يأتي بالمباحثات وبالمندوبات وبالواجبات

words: مَن عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging steadfastness, the next verse encourages fulfilling every Islamic duty through the promise of good life and reward for any believing man or woman doing good.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى رغب المؤمنين في القسم الثاني وهو الإتيان بكل ما كان من شرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although من already conveys generality, naming men and women intensifies the promise and removes any imagined restriction by gender.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية للوعد بالخيرات والمبالغة في تقرير الوعد من أعظم دلائل الكرم والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith differs from righteous action because the verse makes faith a condition for the action's earning reward, and a condition is distinct from what it conditions.
rows.anchor: جعل الإيمان شرطا في كون العمل الصالح موجبا للثواب . وشرط الشيء مغاير لذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī raises an apparent tension: this verse conditions good works' effect on faith, while 99:7 seems to promise an effect for good work without that condition.
rows.anchor: ظاهر قوله : { فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره } يدل على أن العمل الصالح يفيد الأثر سواء كان مع الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the worldly-life interpretation, the discerning believer knows worldly conditions must change and does not cling to them; the ignorant person embraces them and grieves when they vanish, so the believer's life is better.
rows.anchor: العاقل قلبه عليه ولا يقيم له في قلبه وزنا بخلاف الجاهل فإنه يكون غافلا عن هذه المعارف

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī holds that the good life promised here occurs in the grave.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول السدي إن هذه الحياة الطيبة إنما تحصل في القبر

rows.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd b. Jubayr hold that the good life occurs only in the afterlife; 84:6 says human striving continues until meeting the Lord.
rows.anchor: قول الحسن وسعيد بن جبير إن هذه الحياة الطيبة لا تحصل إلا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is life without death, wealth without poverty, health without illness, dominion without loss, and happiness without misery; thus it alone is the good life.
rows.anchor: حياة بلا موت وغنى بلا فقر ، وصحة بلا مرض ، وملك بلا زوال ، وسعادة بلا شقاء

words: وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's closing promise of recompense for the patient repeats the explanation already given above.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى ختم الآية بقوله : { صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون } وقد سبق تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One linguistic explanation takes Ṭā Hā to mean ‘O man’; al-Rāzī accepts it only if the usage belongs to Arabic, since the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic. The cited poem uses Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: إن السفاهة طه في خلائقكم … لا قدس الله أرواح الملاعين

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests that Akkadian Ṭā Hā meaning ‘O man’ may derive from changing yāʾ to ṭāʾ in يا and shortening هذا to ها.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : إن كان طه في لغة عك بمعنى يا رجل فلعلهم تصرفوا في يا هذا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An objector argues that the proposed contraction would have to be written as four letters, طا ها.
rows.anchor: واعترض بعضهم عليه وقالوا : لو كان كذلك لوجب أن يكتب أربعة أحرف طا ها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives a second explanation: Moses stood on one foot in night prayer and was told to place both feet down; طه derives from طأ with hamza changed to hāʾ, as in cited forms هياك and هرقت.
rows.anchor: فأمر أن يطأ الأرض بقدميه معا وكان الأصل طأ فقلبت همزته هاء كما قالوا هياك في إياك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows derivation from وطئ with hamza omitted, yielding طأ يا رجل and a final hāʾ added for pause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأصل من وطىء على ترك الهمزة فيكون أصله طأ يا رجل ثم أثبت الهاء فيها للوقف

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: If Ṭā Hā counts as letter names, the verse begins a new sentence; if it names the sūra, the following clause may predicate of it, with القرآن replacing its pronoun, or answer an oath.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : إن جعلت طه تعديدا لأسماء الحروف فهذا ابتداء كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has ما نزل عليك القرءان instead of ما أنزلنا عليك القرءان.
rows.anchor: قرىء { ما نزل * عليك القرءان لتشقى }

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil reports that Abū Jahl, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī, and al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith said Muhammad suffered for abandoning his fathers' religion; after his answer that he was sent as mercy, they repeated the taunt and the verse rebutted them.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل إن أبا جهل والوليد بن المغيرة ومطعم بن عدي والنضر بن الحارث قالوا لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion is that the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled, and Gabriel told him to spare himself because his body had a right over him.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام صلى بالليل حتى تورمت قدماه فقال له جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same explanation includes a report that the Prophet tied his chest with a rope at night to keep from sleeping; some say he stood on one foot or stayed awake all night.
rows.anchor: وروى أيضا أنه عليه السلام : ( كان إذا قام من الليل ربط صدره بحبل حتى لا ينام )

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the worship-based explanation as unlikely: if the Prophet did these things, they were commanded by God, so they would be happiness rather than something God says He had not commanded.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي هذا بعيد لأنه عليه السلام إن فعل شيئا من ذلك فلا بد وأن يكون قد فعله بأمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading of the address is: do not distress yourself grieving over their disbelief; the Qur'an was sent as a reminder, and each person's belief or unbelief concerns that person, while Muhammad must only deliver.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد لا تشق على نفسك ولا تعذبها بالأسف على كفر هؤلاء فإنا إنما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتذكر به

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that Muhammad is not blamed or held accountable for his people's disbelief once he has conveyed the message.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أنك لا تلام على كفر قومك كقوله تعالى : { لست عليهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this was among the earliest Meccan sūras, when the Prophet was overpowered by enemies, the verse promises that he would not remain humiliated and would rise to honor.
rows.anchor: أن هذه السورة من أوائل ما نزل بمكة وفي ذلك الوقت كان عليه السلام مقهورا تحت ذل أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding statement means God owns the four domains: what is in the heavens, earth, between them, and beneath the moist soil; al-tharā is moist soil, so something may lie below it.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه سبحانه مالك لهذه الأقسام الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning God's enthronement, the passage follows with power and then knowledge: the ownership statement displays power, and 20:7 displays knowledge.
rows.anchor: والملك لا ينتظم إلا بالقدرة والعلم ، لا جرم عقبه بالقدرة ثم بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes أخفى as an intensive or comparative form, dividing what God knows into the spoken aloud, the secret, and the still more hidden.
rows.anchor: إن قوله : { وأخفى } بناء المبالغة ، وعلى هذا القول نقول إنه تعالى قسم الأشياء إلى ثلاثة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most evident sense is that the secret and the more hidden are unspoken matters: God knows what cannot be heard, so He certainly knows what is spoken aloud.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد بالسر وبالأخفى ما ليس بقول وهذا أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible meanings of the hidden levels include a resolve concealed within oneself versus a thought not yet resolved, what is resolved versus an unformed notion, or even what has not yet entered the mind; future divine acts are another possibility.
rows.anchor: والسر هو الذي يسره المرء في نفسه من الأمور التي عزم عليها ، والأخفى هو الذي لم يبلغ حد العزيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī's nearest reading confines secret and hidden matters to what warrants reward or punishment, making the verse a warning against inward and outward sins and an encouragement to inward and outward obedience.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه زجر المكلف عن القبائح ظاهرة كانت أو باطنة ، والترغيب في الطاعات ظاهرة كانت أو باطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse reads أخفى as a verb: God knows people's secrets and has concealed from them what He knows.
rows.anchor: أن أخفى فعل يعني أنه يعلم أسرار العباد وأخفى عنهم ما يعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional can mean that God has no need to hear a loud invocation or other mention because He already knows it.
rows.anchor: إن تجهر بذكر الله تعالى من دعاء أو غيره ، فاعلم أنه غني عن جهرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse discourages loud remembrance, as 7:205 instructs worshippers to remember God inwardly, humbly, fearfully, and without loud speech.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يكون نهيا عن الجهر كقوله : { واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that loud speech serves some other purpose, since it is not needed for God to hear.
rows.anchor: وإما تعليما للعباد أن الجهر ليس لاستماع الله تعالى ، وإنما هو لغرض آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all objects at all times through one unchanging knowledge, an essential attribute of His that is neither originated nor contingent.
rows.anchor: وذلك العلم غير متغير ، وذلك العلم من لوازم ذاته من غير أن يكون موصوفا بالحدوث أو الإمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant's share in knowledge is less than a speck, yet even that tiny share discloses divine attributes; all knowledge ultimately belongs to God because He teaches it, as 4:166 and 67:14 say.
rows.anchor: بل الحق أن الدينار بتمامه له ، لأن الذي علمته فإنما علمته بتعليمه على ما قال : { أنزله بعلمه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the sun illuminating the world without losing any light, God's imparting knowledge does not diminish His own knowledge; nature also shows His detailed awareness of every particle.
rows.anchor: فإن من تدبيراته في خلق الأشجار وأنواع النبات أنها ليس لها فم ولا سائر آلات الغذاء

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question points separately to the staff with تلك and to Moses' hand with بيمينك; God makes each an overpowering sign, elevating inert matter to a miraculous state.
rows.anchor: قوله : { وما تلك } إشارة إلى العصا ، وقوله : { بيمينك } إشارة إلى اليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As inert matter became living and dense matter subtle, God's daily gaze upon a servant's heart can turn disobedient death into obedience and the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى ينظر كل يوم ثلاثمائة وستين نظرة إلى قلب العبد ، فأي عجب لو انقلب قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the staff became a serpent that swallowed the magicians' sorcery, divine attention can make the believer's heart swallow the magic of the commanding soul.
rows.anchor: فأي عجب لو صار القلب بمدد النظر الإلهي بحيث يبتلع سحر النفس الأمارة بالسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the blessing of Moses' right hand made the staff a sign, God's fingers can turn a believer's heart from the darkness of sin to the light of servitude.
rows.anchor: فإذا حصلت ليمين موسى عليه السلام هذه الكرامة والبركة ، فأي عجب لو انقلب قلب المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question does not seek knowledge; it displays the transformation of a lowly object into noble signs and lets Moses first recognize the harmless wooden staff before its transformation.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى لما أراد أن يظهر من العصا تلك الآيات الشريفة كانقلابها حية ، وكضربه البحر حتى انفلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presenting the staff first as a thing that neither harms nor benefits, then turning it into a great serpent, directs minds to God's power and greatness in making great signs from insignificant things.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه قلبه ثعبانا عظيما ، فيكون بهذا الطريق قد نبه العقول على كمال قدرته ونهاية عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first benefit of the question is to introduce an insignificant object before revealing its noble properties, so listeners identify it before the miracle.
rows.anchor: من أراد أن يظهر من الشيء الحقير شيئا شريفا فإنه يأخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' question also teaches that God asks a bewildered believer in the afterlife about what they knew without error in life, namely monotheism, easing their awe and shyness.
rows.anchor: فيسألونه عن الأمر الذي لم يغلط فيه في الدنيا وهو التوحيد ، فإذا ذكره زالت الدهشة والوحشة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks about the staff's uses so Moses names some and then learns it has greater uses than he knew, showing that human reason cannot know all the properties of even a present object without divine guidance.
rows.anchor: فسأله عن منافع العصا فذكر بعضها فعرفه الله تعالى أن فيها منافع أعظم مما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question also establishes firmly for Moses that it is a wooden stick, so he will not fear it when it becomes a serpent.
rows.anchor: فائدة هذا السؤال أن يقرر عنده أنه خشبة حتى إذا قلبها ثعبانا لا يخافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fact that God speaks to Moses does not prove Moses superior to Muhammad: God also addressed Muhammad in 53:10, but kept that speech secret from others.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى كما خاطب موسى فقد خاطب محمدا عليه السلام في قوله : { فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same comparison is answered by noting that Muhammad's community addresses God repeatedly in prayer, and that believers are addressed with greeting and honor in the next life.
rows.anchor: فأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاطبون الله في كل يوم مرات على ما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( المصلي يناجي ربه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī opens a third question asking for the grammatical parsing of وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى, but the segment ends before his answer.
rows.anchor: السؤال الثالث : ما إعراب قوله : { وما تلك بيمينك ياموسى * موسى }
